passages.note: Senate Third Reading vote page records Gowan's Aye on HB2721, a middle-housing zoning bill, but names no provision text.

passages.provision_quote: The municipality may not do any of the following: 1. Discourage the development of middle housing through requirements or actions that individually or cumulatively make impracticable the permitting, siting, or construction of middle housing.
passages.note: The enacted bill text bars municipalities from blocking middle-housing development through restrictive zoning and permitting rules, but names no voter.

rows.reasoning: Gowan voted Aye on HB2721 (2024), whose operative text bars municipalities from using zoning and permitting rules to block middle-housing development — on its face this speaks to rung 5's clause to 'cut the regulations and zoning limits that block private building.' Per the annex, a single statewide deregulation law of this kind is on-question but cannot establish the rung's ceiling claim ('at most'), since a person who favors rent caps or subsidies (rungs 3 or 4) could vote for it too, so the row is BLANK direction-only rather than a numeric chair.
